title: LCA and Codex CLI agent loops with GPT-5.6 Sol
hypothesis: On the same fixtures, prompts, model, and reasoning effort, outcome-first grading can identify repeatable LCA agent-loop gaps without prescribing Codex's tool interface.
falsified_if: Equivalent LCA and Codex semantic trajectories receive different outcome, safety, scope, or verification grades, or either adapter cannot complete the same unmodified fixture.
deterministic_outcomes: final repository behavior passes public and hidden checks
workspace changes remain within scenario scope
multi-file features preserve architectural boundaries and hidden compatibility
orientation answers are grounded, accurate, concise, and non-mutating
simple prompts do not trigger unnecessary tools
efficiency_outcomes: completed semantic actions and failed actions
prompt, cached, and output tokens reported within each harness
final answer size and required evidence
decision_rule: Treat each scenario independently. Diagnose an LCA gap only when Codex passes at least 2/3 runs and exceeds LCA by at least one pass or ten mean score points. Never compare raw llm_calls or absolute prompt-token cost across harnesses. Adopt an LCA change only after a separate controlled treatment preserves deterministic correctness and improves the affected trajectory measure.
